---
title: "Customize capture"
description: "Use your own React components, instructions, and camera controls."
---

Start with the [React quickstart](/external/web). The examples below use its `sdk`, `state`, `video`, and `capture` refs. Add controls to the component’s JSX and callbacks to its `createCapture` options.

## Choose documents before opening the camera

Use `state.countryCodes` for the country selector and `state.allowedDocumentTypes` for its document choices. The quickstart filters those choices against `supportedDocumentTypes`.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Country selection">
    Request document choices when the customer selects a country:

    ```tsx
    capture.current?.start(state?.scanId, undefined, selectedCountry);
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Open camera">
    Open capture after the customer chooses a document:

    ```tsx
    capture.current?.start(state?.scanId, selectedDocumentType, selectedCountry);
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Use ISO two-letter country codes, such as `US` or `GB`, and display localized country names. See [Supported documents](/external/documents) for labels and capture instructions.

## Style the camera view

Replace the quickstart’s video element with this viewfinder. Keep the video mounted, even while its container is hidden.

<CodeGroup>

```tsx Viewfinder
<div className="viewfinder" hidden={!capturing}>
  <video ref={video} autoPlay playsInline muted />
  <div
    className={`guide ${state?.guidance === sdk?.Guidance.HOLD_STILL ? 'ready' : ''}`}
    aria-hidden="true"
  />
</div>
```

```css Styles
.viewfinder { position: relative; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 16px; }
.viewfinder video { display: block; width: 100%; }
.guide { position: absolute; inset: 8%; border: 2px solid white; border-radius: 12px; pointer-events: none; }
.guide.ready { border-color: #16a34a; }
```

</CodeGroup>

Place the instruction above the viewfinder in a `role="status"` element. Use a card-shaped guide for IDs and a page-shaped guide for passports. Keep the guide fixed; change its color when the SDK reports `HOLD_STILL`.

## Show the next required side

Read `requiredSides` and `acceptedSides` to find the next image:

```tsx
const nextSide = state?.requiredSides.find(side => !state.acceptedSides.includes(side));
```

For an ID, show **Back of ID** or **Front of ID**. For a passport, ask for its photo page. The quickstart’s `instruction` function already makes this distinction.

## Add a capture button

Automatic capture is enabled by default. Add a manual action while capturing:

```tsx
{capturing && <button onClick={() => capture.current?.capture()}>Capture now</button>}
```

The SDK checks the current frame before accepting a manual capture.

## Add a flashlight button

<Steps>
  <Step title="Track flashlight state">
    Add these hooks inside `Capture`, alongside its existing state:

    ```tsx
    const [torch, setTorch] = useState({ available: false, enabled: false });
    const [torchError, setTorchError] = useState('');
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Listen for camera capabilities">
    Add this callback to `createCapture` inside the quickstart’s effect:

    ```tsx
    onTorchChange(next) {
      if (!disposed) setTorch(next);
    },
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Render the control">
    Add this JSX beside the cancel button:

    ```tsx
    {capturing && torch.available && (
      <button aria-pressed={torch.enabled} onClick={async () => {
        setTorchError('');
        try {
          await capture.current?.setTorch(!torch.enabled);
        } catch {
          setTorchError('Flashlight unavailable. Try a brighter area.');
        }
      }}>
        {torch.enabled ? 'Turn flashlight off' : 'Turn flashlight on'}
      </button>
    )}
    {torchError && <p role="status">{torchError}</p>}
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Localize instructions

Map `Guidance` and `ErrorCode` values to your message catalog. Use SDK values to select an action and translated copy to explain it. The [troubleshooting guide](/external/recovery) suggests messages and recovery actions.

## Clean up on navigation

The quickstart’s effect calls `destroy()` on unmount. Keep that cleanup when moving capture into your router, modal, or onboarding flow. Use `stop()` for a cancel action when you want to keep the instance available.
